{"command":"create","path":"/workspace/kill_locker.sh","file_text":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DB="/workspace/data.db"
CANDIDATES=("$DB" "${DB}-wal" "${DB}-shm" "${DB}-journal")

find_locking_pids() {
  # Scan /proc for FDs pointing at the DB or its SQLite sidecar files
  for pid_dir in /proc/[0-9]*; do
    pid=${pid_dir#/proc/}
    # Skip if not accessible
    [ -r "$pid_dir/fd" ] || continue
    for fd in "$pid_dir"/fd/*; do
      # Some FDs may disappear while iterating
      target=$(readlink -f "$fd" 2>/dev/null || true)
      for cand in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
        if [ "$target" = "$cand" ]; then
          echo "$pid"
          break
        fi
      done
    done
  done | sort -u
}

pids=$(find_locking_pids || true)
if [ -z "${pids}" ]; then
  echo "No process currently locking $DB (or its -wal/-shm/-journal files)."
  exit 0
fi

echo "Found locker PIDs: $pids"

# Show processes for context
for p in $pids; do
  if [ -r "/proc/$p/cmdline" ]; then
    cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$p/cmdline" || true)
    echo "PID $p -> $cmd"
  else
    echo "PID $p -> <cmdline not readable>"
  fi
done

# Try graceful termination first
if kill -TERM $pids 2>/dev/null; then
  # Wait up to ~5s for them to exit/close the file
  for i in {1..10}; do
    sleep 0.5
    still=$(find_locking_pids || true)
    if [ -z "$still" ]; then
      echo "Lock released after SIGTERM."
      exit 0
    fi
  done
  echo "Some processes still holding the lock after SIGTERM: $still"
else
  echo "Warning: Failed to send SIGTERM to some PIDs (permission?): $pids" >&2
fi

# Force kill as a last resort
if kill -KILL $pids 2>/dev/null; then
  for i in {1..10}; do
    sleep 0.5
    still=$(find_locking_pids || true)
    [ -z "$still" ] && { echo "Lock released after SIGKILL."; exit 0; }
  done
  echo "Warning: Could not release lock even after SIGKILL. Remaining lockers: $still" >&2
  exit 1
else
  echo "Error: Failed to send SIGKILL (permission?). Try running this script with sudo." >&2
  exit 1
fi
"}

message:
I inspected the system and found that /workspace/data.db doesn’t exist here and there’s no process currently holding it open. To let you kill the locker on your machine (where you have sudo), I created a self-contained script that:

- Finds any processes with file descriptors open to /workspace/data.db or its SQLite sidecar files (-wal, -shm, -journal)
- Prints the PIDs and their command lines
- Sends SIGTERM first, waits briefly, then SIGKILL if needed

What I added:
/workspace/kill_locker.sh

How to use:
- Run with sudo on your machine:
  sudo /workspace/kill_locker.sh

Notes:
- If no locker is found, it will print: “No process currently locking /workspace/data.db (or its -wal/-shm/-journal files).”
- If permissions prevent killing, it will prompt to run with sudo.

If you prefer a one-liner (when lsof is available), you can also use:
sudo bash -c 'kill -TERM $(lsof -t -- /workspace/data.db /workspace/data.db-wal /workspace/data.db-shm /workspace/data.db-journal) 2>/dev/null || true'

But the script I added requires no extra tools and should work reliably.
